title: Patent Research Report: Low Acrylonitrile NBR Synthesis
abstract: This report summarizes synthesis-relevant patents for preparing nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) with low acrylonitrile content, focusing on aqueous emulsion polymerization routes.

per_patent_analysis.synthesis_method: Aqueous emulsion polymerization of acrylonitrile and butadiene using a redox initiator system to produce NBR with controlled low ACN content.
example_highlights: Example 1: emulsion copolymerization yielded NBR latex with 18 wt% bound ACN
Example 2: emulsifier level adjusted to stabilize latex at 30% solids
per_patent_analysis.technical_relevance: Directly addresses low-ACN NBR preparation via aqueous emulsion polymerization.

per_patent_analysis.synthesis_method: Cold emulsion copolymerization of acrylonitrile and butadiene with feed-ratio control of bound acrylonitrile.
example_highlights: Example 1: ACN feed adjusted to obtain ~18 wt% bound acrylonitrile in NBR latex
per_patent_analysis.technical_relevance: Provides process details for controlling ACN content during emulsion NBR synthesis.

per_patent_analysis.synthesis_method: Multi-reactor continuous aqueous emulsion polymerization of acrylonitrile and butadiene with surfactant and chain-transfer agent.
disclosed_parameters: Chain transfer agent: used to control molecular weight — Example 2
example_highlights: Example 2: continuous emulsion run with controlled Mooney viscosity
per_patent_analysis.technical_relevance: Industrial continuous emulsion route applicable to low-ACN NBR grades.

cross_patent_comparison: All retained patents use aqueous emulsion polymerization rather than anionic solution routes.
ACN content control is achieved primarily via monomer feed ratio during copolymerization.
Redox or persulfate initiation with anionic emulsifiers is common across examples.
conclusion: The selected patents provide actionable emulsion-polymerization evidence for preparing low acrylonitrile NBR; hydrogenated variants and downstream articles were excluded.
